newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil unveils public sector purchasing bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil unveils public sector purchasing bill.

text.p: The Brazilian government has unveiled a draft bill which lays out new rules for public sector purchasing, contracting and hiring and aims to make the purchasing process faster and more transparent.
The draft bill which was designed and presented by the Federal Administration Ministry on Tuesday, proposes new mechanisms to speed up public tenders including the listing of regular state suppliers.

Federal Administration Minister Luiz Carlos Bresser Pereira said the government is deliberately publicising its proposal in an attempt to generate a public debate and prompt suggestions from existing public sector suppliers and consumer groups.
To that end it has made available two Internet addresses (saur01are.gov.br and ccivil@planalto.gov.br) to gather criticism and suggestions to its proposal.

Government officials estimated public sector purchases account for 16 percent of Brazil's GDP or the equivalent of 120 billion reais ($114 billion) a year. (( -- Adrian Dickson, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5410))
